WoW: Forever

Discipline Priest

Shields and mitigation rather than repair: "there cannot be Light without Dark." The spec is built on Power Word: ShieldPower Word: ShieldLevel 6 · Spell · HolyCastInstantCost45 ManaRange40 yd rangeCooldown4 sec cooldownDuration30 sec — an absorb that stops damage before it lands — and from 25 Soul WardingSoul WardingTalentCastInstant cuts both its cooldown and its Mana cost.

WoW: Forever · Healer · Updated October 5, 2026 · Beta build 1.60.1.70124 · Null Ossuary

Levelling guide, 1 to 60. The beta is capped at level 30 as of the October 1 build, which Blizzard raised from 20 that day, so no level-60 Discipline build has been tested. Talent rows unlock at levels 10, 15, 20, 25, 30, 35 and 40. The one-point milestone talents are gated on points spent, not on level: 11, 21 and 31 points as in Classic, now joined by a new 16-point milestone. No source has posted a level 30 build either — the cap only reached 30 on October 1 and none of the three has published one since — so the level 30 line below extends the published level 20 build using the full talent tree's point costs, not a build any guide has recommended. Blizzard's own September 30, 2026 Class Deep Dive post is folded in below and takes priority over the three guide sites; its own caveat applies: "class abilities and talents may continue to evolve throughout the beta test and are subject to additional changes."

What Discipline is for

Preventing damage instead of repairing it. Power Word: ShieldPower Word: ShieldLevel 6 · Spell · HolyCastInstantCost45 ManaRange40 yd rangeCooldown4 sec cooldownDuration30 sec absorbs the hit before it lands; Soul WardingSoul WardingTalentCastInstant at 25 cuts that shield's cooldown and its Mana cost; Divine AegisDivine AegisTalentCastInstant leaves a fresh absorb behind every critical heal; and from exactly 30 PenancePenanceLevel 30 · Spell · HolyCastInstantCost100 ManaRange40 yd rangeCooldown12 sec cooldown channels damage or healing each second on a 12-second cooldown.

The same mechanic is the solo pattern, and no source scores it — our own reading: shield and wand. Power Word: ShieldPower Word: ShieldLevel 6 · Spell · HolyCastInstantCost45 ManaRange40 yd rangeCooldown4 sec cooldownDuration30 sec absorbs the damage, your wand does the killing, and you spend almost no mana. It is slow and close to unkillable. Discipline has soloed this way since vanilla.

Ratings: Overall 4.5, Levelling 2.5, Dungeon 5.0, Utility 4.0, Mobility 1.0. That 5.0 is the highest dungeon score of any Priest spec, and the 2.5 the second-lowest levelling score of the three. The levelling number measures solo kill speed and nothing else. The published heading is "Struggles To Solo Level": "Discipline Priest has decent single-target damage, but they lack in AoE damage. It's typically recommended to play with a group if you plan to level as Discipline, otherwise it is a better idea to primarily use Shadow talents until you're able to get into group content."

If you are soloing, level Shadow and respec. That is what the guides recommend. Dual Specialization becomes available at level 40, so above that you keep both; below it, respeccing is a trainer visit. In the beta that visit costs 1 silver if you have not changed talents recently, much more for a second reset, and it falls back to 1 silver once an hour has passed — Blizzard calls the price "temporary for the Beta only."

If you are levelling in groups, you do not need to. Discipline is rated 5.0 out of 5 for dungeons, the highest of any Priest spec. The October 1 build cut dungeon quest experience, though — "Dungeon quests now reward 50% less extra experience beyond normal quest values" — so the dungeon route pays less than it did. That a healer finds a group quickly is our own reading, not a published rating.

Your talent points

Level 20: Icy Veins and Wowhead each publish a build, and they do not spend the same 11 points.

Icy Veins' build: Wand SpecializationWand SpecializationTalentCastInstantIncreases your damage with Wands by 13%. 2 → Spirit TapSpirit TapTalentCastInstant 5 (Shadow) → the remaining 4 into Twilight FocusTwilight FocusTalentCastInstantGives you a 70% chance to avoid interruption caused by damage while casting any spell. and/or Improved Power Word: ShieldImproved Power Word: ShieldTalentCastInstantIncreases the damage absorbed by your Power Word: Shield by 20%., whichever you are short on. The first two are called "the most critical" and "the second most important"; Icy Veins does not pin down the exact split of the last 4.

Wowhead's build is the same shape it gives every Priest spec at 20, since the early rows are generic: Wand SpecializationWand SpecializationTalentCastInstantIncreases your damage with Wands by 13%. 2 → Twilight FocusTwilight FocusTalentCastInstantGives you a 70% chance to avoid interruption caused by damage while casting any spell. 3 (Holy tree) → Improved RenewImproved RenewTalentCastInstantIncreases the amount healed by your Renew spell by 5%. 2 → Divine FuryDivine FuryTalentCastInstant 4. No Spirit TapSpirit TapTalentCastInstant, and no Discipline-tree talent beyond the wand point.

ClassicWoW.gg publishes no level-20 point order — its talent page is the full level-60 tree, and it says plainly that this is "the full tree, not a suggested build." Its prose on the damage path: lead with Power in LightPower in LightTalentCastInstantYour Smite and Penance spells deal 15% increased damage to targets afflicted with your Holy Fire. and Holy PrecisionHoly PrecisionTalentCastInstantImproves your chance to hit with Holy spells by 18%. for Holy-spell hit and the Holy Fire/Smite damage bonus, then strengthen those casts with Holy SpecializationHoly SpecializationTalentCastInstantIncreases the critical effect chance of your Holy spells by 1%., Divine FuryDivine FuryTalentCastInstant and Searing LightSearing LightTalentCastInstantIncreases your Holy damage done by 10%, and gives a 10% chance each time your Holy Fire spell deals periodic damage for your next Holy Nova to cost no Mana..

Stat priority

Healing: Healing Power, then MP5, Spirit, Intellect, critical strike — Icy Veins' order.

Critical strike is talked up here where Holy talks it down: Renewed HopeRenewed HopeTalentCastInstant and Divine AegisDivine AegisTalentCastInstant both trigger off healing crits.

Do not itemise Hit for healing gear. Holy PrecisionHoly PrecisionTalentCastInstantImproves your chance to hit with Holy spells by 18%. grants up to 18% Holy spell hit from the talent tree alone, and Blizzard states the intent outright: the talent exists "to remove the need for hit chance on healing Priests, who are not expected to wear gear that increased hit chance."

For the Smite damage build: Spell Power or Holy power, then Hit, Intellect, critical strike. SmiteSmiteLevel 1 · Spell · HolyCast1.5 sec castCost20 ManaRange30 yd rangeSmite an enemy for 15 Holy damage. and Holy FireHoly FireLevel 20 · Spell · HolyCast3.5 sec castCost85 ManaRange30 yd rangeDuration10 sec are Holy-school spells too, so Holy PrecisionHoly PrecisionTalentCastInstantImproves your chance to hit with Holy spells by 18%. chips away at this build's Hit need as well, just without Blizzard's explicit healer framing.

The one-third figure belongs to a talent, not to gear. Spiritual GuidanceSpiritual GuidanceTalentCastInstantIncreases your spell healing by up to 25% of your total Spirit and your spell damage by up to 8% of your total Spirit. in the Holy tree now gives a bonus to spell damage "approximately one third as much as the bonus to spell healing"; nothing in Blizzard's post makes healing bonus on gear grant spell damage.

Sources

Compiled from the three major Forever guide sites and cross-checked against each other. Where Blizzard has published an official class deep dive, that post outranks all three and the page is written from it. Everything else — talent ranks, tooltip values, what exists in the tree at all — is settled against the client itself, read through foreverchanges.pro and wago.tools. Where the guides disagree with each other, this page says which said what.
